production.note: US model years. First: Subaru's release is for the 'All-New 2015 Subaru WRX STI'. Last: Subaru's last WRX STI pricing release is for the 2021 model (subaru-us-2021-wrx-pricing), and its 11 March 2022 statement says "a next generation internal combustion engine WRX STI will not be produced based upon the new WRX platform" (subaru-us-2022-sti-statement). No opened Subaru page says in so many words that 2021 was the last model year.

drivetrain.note: 'Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive with Driver Control Center Differential (DCCD)'

transmission.note: '6-speed manual transmission'; no automatic was offered.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Horsepower 305 @ 6,000 rpm". Also subaru-us-2015-wrx-sti-release: "305 horsepower (SAE) at 6,000 rpm". For 2019 Subaru raised it: "the WRX STI increases horsepower to 310 with the help of a new air intake and high flow performance exhaust" (subaru-us-2019-wrx-sti-release); the 2020 sheet reads "310 @ 6,000 rpm" (subaru-us-2020-wrx-sti-specs). 305 hp is the launch rating and the longer-lived one (2015 to 2018 against 2019 to 2021).

weightLb.note: Base WRX STI, 6-speed manual, 2015 model. Quote: "Curb weight Base: 3,386 lbs Base Harmon Kardon: 3,419 lbs. Premium and Launch Edition: 3,386 lbs. Limited non nav: 3,444 lbs. Limited w/navigation: 3,448 lbs". The 2020 sheet gives 3,450 lb for the base car (subaru-us-2020-wrx-sti-specs).
